title: When Bias Pretends to Be Truth: How Spurious Correlations Undermine Hallucination Detection in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Artificially injecting probabilistic associations between synthetic surnames (e.g., ending in 'kov') and geographic attributes (e.g., Russian birthplaces) into the training dataset to evaluate whether these spurious correlations induce confident hallucinations.

Measuring entity co-occurrence statistics (Jaccard similarity) in the Wikipedia corpus to proxy how strongly associated entities (e.g., the profession 'computer scientist' and the organization 'ACM') induce factual hallucinations on the SimpleQA benchmark.

Controlling the correlation between specific question templates (textual style/structure) and auxiliary attributes (e.g., profession) during supervised fine-tuning to test if models rely on stylistic heuristics rather than factual reasoning.
